title: Option to enable or disable "Automatically enable audio for newly connected devices" behavior
line: Sound settings now have an option to stop newly connected audio devices from becoming the default automatically.
explanation: On PipeWire, WirePlumber picks the default device by priority whenever no chosen default is available, so a USB or Bluetooth device with a higher priority takes over as soon as it is plugged in, and devices remembered from earlier choices take over again when reconnected. The KCM's only related option (switch-on-connect) drives a PulseAudio module and is hidden on PipeWire, so there was no way to turn this off. The change adds an "Automatically switch to newly connected devices" option (on by default) to the KCM's Configure… menu on PipeWire with WirePlumber; when it is off, the plasma-pa kded module sets the current default output and input as the configured default whenever they change, and WirePlumber never moves away from an available configured default.

commits.message:
kcm: add an option to not switch to newly connected devices on PipeWire

WirePlumber always made a newly connected device the default when none
was chosen, and the KCM had no way to turn this off. When the new option
is unchecked, the current default is kept configured instead.

BUG: 516683

media.caption: Sound settings on PipeWire: no Configure… menu, so no way to turn automatic switching off
New Configure… menu with "Automatically switch to newly connected devices", here unchecked
Plugging in a USB headset while the built-in speakers play: the headset becomes the default
Same with the option unchecked: the speakers stay the default, the headset is just listed

review.text: This doesn't change WirePlumber's policy. It rewrites WirePlumber's persisted configured default on every default change, which works around a non-KDE policy and silently changes the user's stored preferences. Because it also pins the fallback device after the configured one is unplugged, reconnecting a headset the user deliberately chose no longer brings it back. Turning the option back on doesn't undo what it pinned.
changes: Don't re-pin when the default changed because the configured device went away (fallback); only prevent a newly added device from taking over, so a user-chosen device still returns when reconnected.
Ask WirePlumber upstream for a policy setting (no auto-switch to new devices) and link it in the MR; keep the Plasma side as a thin toggle of that setting where available.
